subject: Model V7Y p95 drift — proposed traffic throttle & fallback variant
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@bluecresthealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodelabs.com>
Cc: support@bluecresthealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: p95 spike observed on Model V7Y in production

Hi Hannah,

Quick heads up — our telemetry shows a sudden jump in p95 latency for requests hitting Model V7Y (production). Baseline p95 has been ~180ms for the past week; starting ~07:45 PT today p95 climbed to ~740ms and has stayed high. Throughput and error rates look nominal; we're seeing elongated tail token generation only on that model.

We tried routing a small subset of traffic to the v7y-quant variant and saw p95 drop back toward baseline within the sample window. I attached the CSV with the p95 snapshots and a short span of request ids for trace.

Can you confirm whether there was a rollout or config change to V7Y overnight on Redwood's side? Our production is sensitive to latency — this is starting to impact our UX.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Platform Engineering | Bluecrest Health
Attachments: p95_snapshot-20280115.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: p95 spike observed on Model V7Y in production

Thanks for flagging, Samir — and sorry for the impact.

Internal team: please triage urgently. Initial asks:
- Confirm whether the V7Y rollout that completed 01:00 PT introduced any kernel/quant changes for long context workloads.
- Check canary results and whether a subset of hosts is experiencing memory pressure or GC spikes.
- If we can reproduce quickly, propose a rollback of the flagged rollout or route a percentage of traffic to v7y-quant fallback.

Operational proposal for approval:
- Immediate temporary traffic throttle: shift up to 20% of Bluecrest traffic off V7Y to v7y-quant while we triage (target p95 recovery).
- If triage shows a bad kernel, authorize a canary rollback for the recent build across the cluster.

Marcus — do you approve the temporary throttle + fallback? Karthik/Neha — can you start the triage and collect kernel traces/log bundle (attach) and open a short-lived JIRA with remediation steps?

I'll keep Samir updated and coordinate comms.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Approved.

Proceed with:
1) Immediate 20% traffic shaping for Bluecrest (route to v7y-quant).
2) Canary rollback of the 01:00 PT artifact if root cause points to the new kernel path.
3) Post-mit postmortem and a customer note summarizing the timeline + remediation.

Karthik — FYI I want a quick impact estimate if we keep the throttle for >4 hours (cost & unit throughput). Open INF-3321 and tag ops-owner.

Marcus

On Mon, Jan 15, 2028 at 09:18, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Approved.
>
> Proceed with:
> 1) Immediate 20% traffic shaping for Bluecrest (route to v7y-quant).

Update from triage: early signals point to a kernel path regression in the attention op triggered at sequence lengths >1024 — memory pressure on nodes running the latest build. Reproduced locally against a replay of the Bluecrest sample; switching to the quantized variant removes the pathological allocation pattern.

Actions taken (so far):
- Activated the traffic shift to v7y-quant at 10:45 PT (approx 15% of live Bluecrest traffic diverted). Config snapshot attached (canary-traffic-config.json).
- Opened INF-3321 and attached kernel traces.
- Kicked an automated canary rollback pipeline for the midnight artifact; monitoring rollback results now.

I'll follow up with a short remediation playbook and ETA once rollback completes.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: p95 spike observed on Model V7Y in production

Samir — thanks for the quick report and patience. Short summary and plan for Bluecrest: 

1) Symptoms: p95 rise from ~180ms -> ~740ms starting ~07:45 PT; error rates unchanged.
2) Immediate mitigation: ~15% of traffic routed to v7y-quant; observed p95 recovery in the sample window.
3) Engineering action: canary rollback triggered for the recent artifact; kernel traces collected and INF-3321 opened for remediation.
4) Next steps for you: we will keep the fallback in place while rollback completes and monitor for 1 hour after rollback to confirm p95 stability. We expect a full resolution or targeted patch within the next 4 hours; if that slips we'll propose a longer-lived traffic carveout and provide a customer-facing timeline.

We understand the SLA sensitivity here — I'm prioritizing post-mit comms and a short incident report when this is resolved. Please let me know if you want a live sync (we can join your ops channel).

Hannah
